request.system:
You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, the section look, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and name them in `present` by their ids; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id in `present` so its canon constraints reach the image model. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own poses, clothing and actions; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them. Use the canon as constraints, without copying its fixed description into the plan.
request.user:
WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: The Ancient of Days and the son of man
SECTION LOOK: place: Heavenly court above Babylon, vast open expanse of cloud and radiant fire; time: Night vision, sky of unbroken darkness; weather: Stormy air with drifting clouds and fire; light: Radiant fiery glow from the throne and wheels, no visible sun; clothing: Daniel in a simple Babylonian-era tunic and cloak; court attendants in plain robes. The formless divine presence has no body, hair or garments.
CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- daniel_prophet_of_babylon: Daniel (prophet of Babylon) (hasForm: true)
- the_ancient_of_days: The Ancient of Days (hasForm: false)
- one_like_a_son_of_man: One like a son of man (hasForm: true)
- babylon: Babylon (hasForm: true)

NO-FORM CANON CONSTRAINTS (planning context; fixed descriptions are not scene-plan fields):
- the_ancient_of_days (stage: the_ancient_of_days-showing): The Ancient of Days: brilliant white radiance; bright orange fire; soft white cloud; brilliant white light.

MOMENT (Daniel 7:9): “I watched until thrones were placed, and one who was Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
PREVIOUS: (section starts here)
NEXT: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him. Thousands of thousands ministered to him. Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The judgment was set. The books were opened.

present.description: IDs of section cast present in this moment, including no-form subjects represented through their permitted effects. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or merely mentioned.

primarySubject.description: The main subject's visible effect and placement, or a formed character's situational pose. For a seated no-form metaphor, describe an unoccupied seat with permitted effects around it. Example: light spreading above an unoccupied seat; the witness looks up. Use canon as constraints rather than restating fixed appearance. At most 220 characters.

action.description: What formed characters do and how permitted environmental effects move or change in this moment. Keep formed characters' own actions and any situational clothing attached to them. At most 220 characters.

setting.description: The physical place, surfaces and surroundings of this single scene, consistent with the section look and era. At most 220 characters.

secondaryElements.description: Supporting people, props and permitted environmental effects with their placement. Describe effects directly rather than using bodily or garment substitutes for a no-form subject. At most 220 characters.

mood.description: The emotional atmosphere of this moment, conveyed through the setting and formed characters' reactions. At most 220 characters.

timeOfDay.description: This moment's time of day and situational illumination, consistent with the section look. At most 220 characters.

composition.description: Viewpoint, framing and relative placement of formed subjects, objects and permitted effects in one scene. Keep this independent of art style and rendering technique. At most 220 characters.

payload.name: The Ancient of Days
payload.note: The divine figure on a fiery throne in Daniel's vision of the beasts; a distinct visionary figure, seen only in Daniel's dream-vision.

stages.label: The Ancient of Days
stages.text: The Ancient of Days: brilliant white radiance; bright orange fire; soft white cloud; brilliant white light.

quotes.quote: His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool.
His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
A fiery stream issued and came out from before him.

payload.name: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)
payload.note: The Jewish youth taken captive to Babylon, renamed Belteshazzar, who interprets dreams and receives visions; the main entry with many sections in Daniel, distinguished from the prophet named only in Matthew's citation.

stages.label: Daniel (Belteshazzar), prophet of Babylon

quotes.quote: Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar
he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem)

stages.text: Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man in his youth grown to a grave, graying elder; olive-brown skin; dark hair cropped close and a short trimmed beard flecked with grey; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.

aliases: one like a son of man
payload.name: One like a son of man
payload.note: The figure coming with the clouds of heaven to receive dominion in Daniel's vision; not the Gospel Jesus, but a distinct heavenly figure in Daniel.

stages.label: One like a son of man

quotes.quote: there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days

stages.text: One like a son of man: a man in his prime, early thirties, of athletic but dignified build; skin warm olive-brown; short dark hair and a close-cut beard; calm, steady features with a grave, luminous gaze. He wears a long white linen tunic with a deep blue-purple cloak falling from the shoulders, edged with gold thread. He carries no props.

payload.name: Babylon
payload.note: The city and empire of exile and captivity across the prophets, histories and psalms, also called Babylonia, Shinar and the land of the Chaldeans; the same place in every division.

stages.label: Babylon

quotes.quote: The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown. Her high gates will be burned with fire.
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up.
He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me.

stages.text: Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.

payload.name: Elisha son of Shaphat
payload.note: Prophet, Elijah's successor, who first appears as a farmer plowing with twelve yoke of oxen in 1 Kings and is later named in 2 Kings and Luke; the same prophet in all three entries.

stages.label: Elisha son of Shaphat

quotes.quote: found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him
Elijah went over to him and put his mantle on him.
He took Elijah’s mantle that fell from him
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by the way, some youths came out of the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!”

stages.text: Elisha son of Shaphat: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sun-browned from working the fields, lean and steady in build. Dark skin, a bald head, and a close-cut beard with some grey at the chin. Calm, weathered face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of rough brown wool. Signature prop: Elijah's mantle, a dark sheepskin cloak he wears over his shoulders.
